tldr: Each subscription webhook gets a payloadGeneration setting. DEFERRED builds its payload in a background task. IMMEDIATE builds it during the request or task that triggers the event.
goal: Some apps need a payload that reflects the object's state at the event, not at the later task run.

story.heading: Webhooks choose when their payload is built
story.body: Subscription webhooks split into deferred and immediate groups before the payload is built.

story.heading: GraphQL API exposes the payload generation setting
story.body: Webhook create, update and trigger accept a payloadGeneration value, DEFERRED or IMMEDIATE.

story.heading: Webhook table stores the payload generation
story.body: The webhook table adds a payload_generation field. Existing webhooks keep the deferred behavior.

story.heading: Apps set the setting in their manifests
story.body: Manifest webhooks accept payloadGeneration. A missing value means DEFERRED. Other values fail validation.

components.summary: Adds the WebhookPayloadGeneration enum and the payloadGeneration argument on webhook mutations.
Reads payloadGeneration from app manifests and maps the enum name to the stored value.
Groups subscription webhooks by payload generation and builds immediate payloads during the event.

decisions.title: Keep DEFERRED as the default payload generation
decisions.why: Existing webhooks keep their current behavior, and the payload is built in a background task.

decisions.title: Build immediate payloads in the request that triggers the event
decisions.why: The payload then reflects the object's state at the event, at the cost of slowing that request or task.
decisions.alternative: Build all payloads in the deferred task

decisions.title: Split webhooks by setting before the payload is built
decisions.why: Each group takes its own build path, so the trigger code stays the same for both.
decisions.alternative: Check the setting for each webhook inside the trigger loop

flows.title: Send an order event to apps
